currentContext.expansion: Expansion in FY26 was driven by inorganic moves rather than greenfield capacity. Subsequent to the reporting period the Board approved the acquisition of a 78.26% equity stake in Advent Coal Resources Pte. Ltd., Singapore - which owns the MEC Coal Project in Indonesia along with associated logistics infrastructure - with the entire purchase consideration discharged through issuance of equity shares; and a 50.10% equity stake in Sainik Mining and Allied Services Limited, an Indian mine development and overburden removal contractor and a related party, with consideration discharged through issuance of Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares. Members approved both on June 18, 2026 and in-principle approvals were received from BSE and NSE on July 31, 2026; as at the date of the Board's Report the Company was circulating the Form PAS-4 offer letter to identified investors under the share-swap terms. The two deals, together valued at over Rs. 922 crores, were funded through preferential issuances of equity shares and compulsorily convertible preference shares and are intended to move the Company up the value chain from logistics and trading into direct mining assets. Organic capital spending remained fleet-led: BRSR Principle 2 records that investments were made by way of addition to capital assets in the form of Loaders & Tippers and Excavators, with the Company owning a fleet of more than 200 Tippers and 100 Loaders and operating more than 600 Tippers and Loaders including leased and attached vehicles. Growth in the Indonesian coal mining business is stated to be fuelled by a significant aspirational ramp-up in coal mine production supported by thermal power demand and planned investment in infrastructure expansion. No greenfield plant, commissioning date or rupee capex quantum is disclosed; BRSR Section A reports zero plants and nine national offices.

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.
